subject.title: feat(sessions): upstream liveness for adopted catalog sessions

question: Should the permanent Plugin SDK expose a generic opaque upstream-session probing contract now, or should provider-specific liveness remain internal until the broader SessionObserver design is approved?
rationale: The PR adds compatibility-sensitive public SDK types and a provider hook, while the current closed source-kind union and core-exported Claude classification conflict with the repository's plugin ownership boundary; code review cannot choose that permanent API direction.

options.title: Adopt an opaque generic contract
options.body: Make source identity and marker payloads plugin-defined, retain only generic agent-qualified activity semantics in core, and keep Claude/Codex classification in their owner plugins.

options.title: Defer the public SDK seam
options.body: Keep this feature provider-internal or pause the PR until the broader SessionObserver API and compatibility policy are explicitly sponsored.

options.title: Sponsor the current fixed contract
options.body: Accept the closed source-kind union and core classification exports as permanent SDK surface with explicit compatibility documentation and focused external-plugin tests.

recommendation.title: Adopt an opaque generic contract
recommendation.body: Make source identity and marker payloads plugin-defined, retain only generic agent-qualified activity semantics in core, and keep Claude/Codex classification in their owner plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged session-state work and the canonical observed-session design issue provide the strongest available ownership trail for this product/API choice.
